newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. briefs Israel on Iraqi action.
newsitem.headline: U.S. briefs Israel on Iraqi action.

text.p: U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk briefed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday minutes after the Pentagon said it had launched a missile attack against Iraq, witnesses said.

Witnesses said Indyk entered the prime minister's office about a half hour after the United States said it had launched cruise missile attacks against air defence targets to retaliate for Iraqi attacks in the Kurdish north.
Sources at the U.S. embassy in Tel Aviv said Indyk received instructions from the White House to brief the Israeli leader. Israel said Indyk would later meet Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy.
Baghdad launched dozens of Scud missile attacks against Israel when fighting a U.S.-led alliance against Iraq during the 1991 Gulf War. Washington is Israel's closest ally.

The United States last sent cruise missiles against Iraq in June 1993 to avenge an alleged plot to kill former U.S. president George Bush during a visit to Kuwait. The attacks then killed six civilians.
